comments.author: @mshonle
comments.text:
These interacting LLMs can perform better at tasks, but another benefit I see is how interaction increases explainability. Asking GPT “how” it came up with an answer has no correlation to the actual neural activations, but having the “paper trail” of agent interactions (plus knowing how each agent has been fine tuned) leads to plausible explanations.

I’d love to see something like this played out where 16 agents are each fine tuned according to the Myers-Briggs Type Indicators (the MBTI system has been criticized in terms of psychological value, but it’s still a useful tool for authors trying to create new characters). Having more neural pathways active might lead to more rogue characters, so pruning and re-rolling the dice might be needed. Speaking of dice rolling, it would be interesting to see if changing the temperatures of different agents at different times could lead to more productive searches when they are in a rut. (Perhaps then Bob could have realized two cows were sufficient to obtain three leathers because you could breed and grow more cows once you have two and some hay.)

The problem with any tech company in China working on cutting-edge technology such as AI is that the CCP has a long history of coming in and snatching up these companies and then using their technology to further their own agenda which is often very anti-humanitarian. We have seen how good first-generation machine learning is at psychologically profiling people, such as the way the Google algorithm will target you with very personalized ads.
